page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.4-16 is a virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.25 GHz. It is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores that execute 2 threads per core, yielding 8 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) alongside 16.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a compute-skewed allocation ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring the use of remote block storage volumes for persistent data and operating system installations. It contains zero GPU accelerators. Networking provisions include one complimentary public IPv4 address for external network connectivity.

With its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the VM.Standard.E3.Flex.4-16 is tailored for workloads that require dedicated processing threads without high per-thread memory capacity. Appropriate deployments include continuous integration build agents, containerized web servers, distributed application nodes, and moderate batch processing workflows.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.4-16 is an x86_64 virtual instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor running at 2.25 GHz. It provides 4 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled, delivering 8 vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory. This resource profile yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, allocating 2.0 GB of memory per execution thread. The instance contains no integrated local storage or GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage for persistent workloads. Network capabilities include one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server is configured for CPU-centric tasks where memory requirements are moderate, making it suitable for web serving, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and general batch execution.
